current_answer: Awesome Foundation DC presents a local cash-grant route for individual project applicants: USD 1,000 no-strings-attached awards, usually selected monthly. The DC chapter says a project must directly benefit Washington, DC, make a real difference with USD 1,000, and be ready to act soon. It is a discretionary project grant, not a general startup budget or personal-expense payment; the reviewed page does not publish a precise current submission cutoff, residency rule, selection rate, or award guarantee.

catalogue_card.question: Have a DC project? This USD 1,000 grant needs a near-term outcome.
catalogue_card.text: Awesome Foundation DC shows a monthly USD 1,000 cash-grant application for projects that directly benefit Washington, DC. The chapter wants a project USD 1,000 can materially advance soon. Its page does not publish a precise current cutoff, residency rule, selection rate, or award guarantee, so check the live form before applying.

summary: Awesome Foundation DC currently shows an application route for a USD 1,000 no-strings-attached local project grant.
The chapter says it weighs direct benefit to Washington, DC, whether USD 1,000 makes an actual impact, and whether the project is immediately actionable, generally within one or two months.
The chapter says it focuses on individuals and small groups with new, small projects and usually selects winners at the end of each month.

This is a discretionary project grant, not a general startup budget or payment for personal expenses. The reviewed page does not publish a precise current cutoff, residency rule, selection rate, or award guarantee.
GitHub’s Student Developer Pack Stripe and Heroku offers remain separate student routes; neither turns a fee or hosting credit into cash.
uncertainty: Awesome Foundation DC does not publish an exact current application closing time, residency requirement, selection rate, or award guarantee; it says winners are usually selected at the end of each month.
GitHub's public Stripe Pack entry does not publish Stripe country or account eligibility, exact covered fees and products, redemption steps, expiry, or fees after the USD 25 credit.
GitHub says third-party Pack offers may change and some may not be repeated or stacked with a partner free trial; check the live Stripe claim before setting up payments.
Heroku's public Student Developer Pack entry does not publish country availability, plan coverage, monthly-credit rollover, a card requirement, or the price after credits.
Oracle makes the US$300 trial available only in select countries, and exact Free Tier availability can differ during sign-up.
Oracle Cloud Free Tier capacity limits can prevent a particular resource from being provisioned in the chosen Home Region.

Microsoft's current direct-path documentation conflicts on the starter amount: the application guide says USD 200, while the activation guide says USD 1,000. The issuer has not published a reconciliation, so the direct starter amount is Unknown until the account flow shows it.
Cloudflare Tier 3 still pairs “bootstrapped or self-funded” with a programme-wide “funded within the last 12 months” condition; the issuer has not reconciled the terms.
DigitalOcean does not publish a fixed direct-applicant award, country-availability map, review time, or applicant-specific GPU-credit outcome.
Individual-grant coverage is still narrow and not a worldwide inventory.
